akhfash:3-3.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِراً وَإِمَّا كَفُوراً ﴾; likewise ﴿إِمَّا ٱلعَذَابَ وَإِمَّا ٱلسَّاعَةَ﴾: it is as if you had not mentioned "إمَّا" ("either"); and if you wish, you begin afresh with what follows it and make it nominative.

akhfash:6-6.t: And He said ﴿عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He made it accusative in three ways. If you wish, it is on His words ﴿يَشْرَبُونَ﴾ [5] "﴿عَيْناً﴾" ("they drink … a spring"); if you wish, on ﴿يَشْرَبُونَ مِن كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُوراً﴾ ﴿عَيْناً﴾; and if you wish, by way of praise (madḥ), as when a man mentions someone to you and you say "العاقلَ واللبيبَ" ("the intelligent one, the discerning one!"), that is: you have mentioned the intelligent, discerning one — on the pattern "أَعْنِي عَيْناً" ("I mean a spring").

akhfash:9-9.t: [And He said] ﴿وَلاَ شُكُوراً﴾: if you wish, you make it the plural of "الشُكْر" (thanks), and make "الكُفُور" the plural of "الكُفْر" (ingratitude), like "الفَلْس" and "الفُلُوس". And if you wish, you make it a single maṣdar (verbal noun) with a plural meaning, like "قَعَد قُعُودا" and "خَرَج خُروجا".

akhfash:13-14.t: And He said ﴿مُّتَّكِئِينَ﴾: by way of praise (madḥ), or on "جَزَاهُمْ جَنَّةً مَتُكَّئِيِنَ فيها" ("He rewarded them with a garden, reclining in it") as a ḥāl (circumstantial). And you may say "جَزاَهُم ذلكَ قِياماً" ("He rewarded them with that, standing"). Likewise ﴿وَدَانِيَةً﴾ is a ḥāl or by way of praise; its accusative is only due to an implied verb. It is also permissible in His words ﴿وَدَانِيَةً﴾ for it to be on two aspects: on "وجزاهمْ دانيةً ظِلاَلُها" ("and He rewarded them with [a garden] whose shades are near"), as you say "اَعطَيْتُكَ جَيْداً طَرَفاهُ" ("I gave you one whose two ends are good") and "رأينَا حَسَناً وَجْهُهُ" ("we saw one whose face is handsome"). «[Translator's note: only one of the "two aspects" is spelled out in the source.]»

akhfash:17-17.t:
And He said ﴿كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنجَبِيلاً﴾: He made "the spring" (العين) accusative in four ways: on "يُسْقَوْنَ عَيْناً" ("they are given a spring to drink"), or as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or as a badal (substitute) for "the cup", or by way of praise (madḥ), the verb being implied. Some said that "سلسبيل" is a description (ṣifa) of the spring, describing it as «سَلْسَبِيل». And some said: "He only meant 'a spring that is named «سَلْسَبِيل»' (عَيْناً تُسَمَّى سَلْسَبِيلاً)", that is: it is so called because of its excellence, that is: it is described (thus) to people, just as you say "الأعوجيّ" and "الأَرْحَبِيّ" and "المَهْرِيّ من الإِبل" (the Mahrī among camels); and just as horses, when described, are attributed to these well-known, pedigreed horses, so likewise the spring is attributed by being named [«سَلْسَبِيل»], because the Qur'an points to the speech of the Arabs. The poet said — and Yūnus recited it to us thus — [in the kāmil metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-fourth verse cited as evidence]:
صَفْراءُ مِنْ نَبْعٍ يُسَمَّى سَهْمُها * مِنْ طُولِ ما صَرَعَ الصُّيُودَ الصَّيِّبُ
(A yellow [bow] of nabʿ wood, whose arrow is called — from how long it has felled the game — "the sure-hitter".)
He put "الصيِّب" in the nominative because he did not mean "its arrow is named 'the sure-hitter'" (يسمى سهمها بالصيِّب); rather "الصيِّب" is a description of the name and of the arrow. And his words "يسمى سهمها" mean: its arrow is spoken of. And some said: "No, rather it is the name of the spring, and it is definite; but since it is the end of a verse [and] it had fatḥa, you added the alif to it, as with ﴿قَوَارِيرَاْ﴾."

akhfash:20-20.t: And He said ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيماً﴾: He means to make "رأَيْتَ" not take an object (intransitive), as one says "ظننت في الدار خيرٌ" ("I supposed: in the house there is good") on account of the place of his supposing; and He reported the place of his seeing.
